CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD
ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 18.07.2019 passed by the VIII Additional SCJ & XXXIII ACMM, Member-MACT, Bengaluru in MVC No.6511/2017.

entities.text: VIII Additional SCJ & XXXIII ACMM, Member-MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that 05.07.2017 at about 3.40 p.m.,
the claimant was riding his motor cycle bearing Registration No.KA-52-K-6374 slowly and cautiously by following the traffic rules on left side of the road on NH-4, Tumkur- Bengaluru Highway, near Huchegowdanapalya, Kasaba NC: 2024:KHC:32360 Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru Rural District.

At that time, the driver of the lorry bearing Registration No.HR- 74-A-5241 drove the same in rashly, recklessly and negligently with high speed endangering human life and property and dashed against the back side of the claimant's motorcycle.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32360 respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The claimant, in order to prove the case, examined himself as PW-1, another witness was examined as PW-2 and Dr.Nagaraj B.N. was examined as PW-3, and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
On behalf of the respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R7.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned Suresh K N vs Sri. Abbas on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173757143/
2 judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

entities.text: Suresh K N vs Sri. Abbas
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,11,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with NC: 2024:KHC:32360 interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimant has examined the doctor as PW- 3.
The doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant has suffered disability of 43% to right arm and 14% to the whole body.
But the compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'loss on account of disability' is on lower side.
b) Secondly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 15 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.

Considering the same, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings'
and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
Thirdly, the doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant requires about Rs.50,000/- for removal of implants.
But the Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head of 'future medical expenses'.
With the above contentions, learned counsel for the appellant sought to allow the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:
a) Firstly, even though the doctor testified that the claimant has suffered a 14%
disability to the whole body, this disability has not resulted in any loss of income.
Notably, the claimant has continued to work after the accidental injuries without any decrease in salary.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly not granted any compensation under the head of loss of future income.

b) Secondly, considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and considering the age and avocation of the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under NC: 2024:KHC:32360 the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings' and other incidental expenses are just and reasonable and it does not warrant interference.

3 c)

sentences.text: Thirdly, although the doctor has stated that the claimant requires Rs.50,000/- for future medical expenses, no estimate has been provided.
Therefore, the Tribunal has correctly not awarded any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

d) Lastly, in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Venkateshan.V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount appears excessive.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the above contentions, learned counsel for the Insurance Company sought to dismiss the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
NC: 2024:KHC:32360 9.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 05.07.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
10. As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained fracture of the right greater Tuberosity of the Humerus.

The doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant has suffered disability of 43%
to right arm and 14% to the whole body.
The claimant has not suffered any loss of future income due to the said disability, as he has continued to work in his job.

Therefore, taking into consideration the deposition of the doctor, injuries mentioned in the wound certificate, age and avocation, I am of the opinion that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'loss on account of disability' is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
11. Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also undergone surgery.
He was NC: 2024:KHC:32360 hospitalized as an inpatient for more than 15 days in the hospital.

Considering the prolonged pain during treatment as well as the permanent disability certified by the doctor, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and sufferings' from Rs.50,000/- to Rs.75,000/- and under the head of 'loss of amenities' from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
12.
Although the evidence of the doctor suggests that the claimant requires approximately Rs.50,000/- for removal of implants, the claimant has not provided an estimate for future surgery.

Considering the nature of the injuries and the evidence of the doctor, I am inclined to award the compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of 'future medical expenses'.
13.
Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.

ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.

d) Following the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE'
